storylines.label: DeepSeek V4.1-Flash
storylines.latest_title: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash Prices Cached Input To $0.003 Per Million Tokens

prior_narrative.tldr: DeepSeek unveiled V4.1-Flash on Sep 10, claiming it beats its own flagship V4-Pro while cutting the memory agents need to run it. By Sep 11 the release was already squeezing rivals on price.
prior_narrative.whats_new: DeepSeek is now routing all V4-Pro API traffic to V4.1-Flash under the hood, billing it at V4.1-Flash's lower rate rather than V4-Pro's.
prior_narrative.why_it_matters: Anyone calling the V4-Pro endpoint is now served different weights than they pinned, at a different price, without a version bump to signal it.
prior_narrative.take_for_builders: Re-run your eval suite against the V4-Pro endpoint now: you're getting V4.1-Flash's outputs, and any prompt or behavior tuned to V4-Pro specifically may have silently drifted.

status.detail: V4.1-Flash shipped Sep 10 claiming to beat V4-Pro on quality while cutting agent memory needs; by Sep 14 DeepSeek was routing all V4-Pro API calls to V4.1-Flash at Flash rates instead of retiring or renaming the endpoint.

beats.headline: DeepSeek unveils V4.1-Flash, claims it beats flagship V4-Pro
beats.summary: The new model launches as an upgrade over DeepSeek's own current flagship.

beats.headline: Cuts the memory footprint agents need to run it
beats.summary: Coverage frames the release around lower memory needs specifically for agentic use.

beats.headline: Early pricing pressure on rivals, then a v5-caliber technical reception
beats.summary: The release moves competitor pricing within a day, and technical reviewers rate the architecture jump higher than a point release.

beats.headline: DeepSeek quietly swaps V4-Pro traffic for V4.1-Flash at Flash pricing
beats.summary: Four days after launch, calls to the V4-Pro endpoint are served by V4.1-Flash instead, billed at the cheaper Flash rate.

open_questions: Does the claimed memory-footprint cut hold up in independent agent-workload benchmarks, not just DeepSeek's own claim?
Will DeepSeek formally deprecate the V4-Pro endpoint, or keep serving V4.1-Flash under the old name indefinitely?
Do outputs from the V4-Pro endpoint show measurable quality or behavior differences now that V4.1-Flash serves them?

day_captions.3964e6fc7e6673d5: First outlet to frame the release around agent memory costs specifically.
day_captions.82bd95dd18d293f1: First sign the release is already moving competitor pricing.
day_captions.d1d28ac13afc9a24: AINews' technical deep dive frames the architecture as v5-caliber.
day_captions.7f7e6754ebc2c737: DeepSeek starts serving all V4-Pro API traffic with V4.1-Flash, at Flash's lower price.
